# Risks and open items: printer_v8

Generated by `tools/build_package.py` from `designs/printer_v8.py` (md5 `9f4017d87957e199a7069390d97496bc`) and `out/printer_v8/report.json` (written 2026-11-15 18:53:15, md5 `1d5bf219132d`). Do not edit: change the design, re-run verify, re-run the generator.

> **Simulated design. Nothing has been built.** See [OPEN_ITEMS.md](OPEN_ITEMS.md) before spending money.

## What this package is

**This is a simulated design. It has never been built.** It passes 12 of 12 verifiers of `mechloop` with 0 errors and 13 warnings. A pass means the model is consistent with the checks that exist; it does not mean the machine works. The checks have known limits, quoted here from `AGENT.md` ('Not checked'):

> Bolt preload and contact (stiffness is bracketed, not predicted), fatigue, buckling, the
> thermal behaviour of a part while it prints (warping is a rule of thumb only), belt tooth load and what belt
> tension does to belt stiffness (only the pull on a motor shaft is checked), stall detection in sensorless homing,
> cable paths (only lengths), axial
> retention of bearings, closed kinematic loops, curved insertion paths, cables,
> real manufacturing cost (the estimate is rough) and tolerances a process can hold on a feature. FEA is linear static with idealised
> fixtures and no self-weight; assemblies are bonded, which overstates stiffness.
> Guide moments are estimates. Catalog ratings are typical values.
> 
> Clearance under tolerance: gaps drawn wider than 1.5 mm are not examined (a finding says when a chain scatters more
> than that); the gap is judged along its drawn direction only (an edge sliding past a corner is not); adjustments are
> not credited (the share is as built, before anything is set), except Z homing on the bed. Bent parts: springback
> along a bend and twist are not modelled. Bed support: nut axial stiffness and backlash, block stiffness sideways and
> about the rail, belt synchronisation error and the rail accuracy class are assumed and said so in the metrics; the
> straightness of the extrusion a rail is screwed to is not catalogued and not included; the silicone bed columns are
> meshed with the catalogue's stand-in rubber (real silicone is softer).
> Several lead screws on one Z are NOT supported by: the digital twin (it models one Z drive: travel per turn and
> summed motor torque, no tilt between screws); the motion verifier's dynamics (one joint, one effort); a generated
> `[z_tilt]` from geometry (you state z_positions and points); `quad_gantry_level`; and the catalogue has no board with
> more than four drivers (SKR Mini E3 V3.0: X, Y, Z, E), so independent Z motors beyond the one driver cannot be wired
> from catalogue parts, and no integrated lead-screw motor (the one vendor record, StepperOnline 17E19S1684MB4-300RS,
> holds only screw diameter and lead: holding torque, current, resistance, inductance, rotor inertia, mass, body and
> nut dimensions and thrust rating are missing).

Counts: 17 A, 24 B, 19 C. Ranking is the generator's judgement (rules and a curated list in `tools/build_package.py`); the numbers in each item are read from the report.

## Needed from the design

Data this package wanted and neither the design file nor the catalogue holds. Nothing was hard-coded in its place.

| What | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| the design file's hash inside report.json (written by `mechloop verify`) | staleness can only be inferred: from part count, mass, BOM and custom-part list, from the md5 quoted in docs/<NAME>.md, and from the previous package's manifest. A design edit that changes none of these (a hole moved) is not detected on a first run |
| fold-back length of each open belt end in its anchor | cut length of the X and Y belts = path length + two anchors; only the path is modelled |
| print settings per printed part (layer height, wall count, infill) | strength results assume solid material; the estimate assumed 1.2 mm walls / 20 % infill |
| steel grade and finish for the laser-cut steel parts | material 'steel' is a generic entry (E 200 GPa, yield 250 MPa); no corrosion protection is specified |
| tightening torque per fastener class | the assembly guide can only say 'snug' |
| T-nut type (drop-in or slide-in) and when each is inserted | slide-in T-nuts must be loaded before a slot is closed off; the assembly simulation does not contain T-nuts |

### The designer's own list (quoted from docs/PRINTER_V8.md)

| Part | What is missing | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Spring-steel print sheet, 220 mm | thickness, steel grade, mass, a part number | probe distance, bed mass |
| Magnetic sheet | thickness, mass, temperature limit, adhesive | the 80 degC bed limit |
| OMRON E2E-X5ME1 | sensing distance on a thin spring-steel sheet (the 5 mm is for 1 mm iron, 15 x 15 mm), repeatability | the whole probe window |
| GT2 closed belt, 6 mm | stock lengths near 1,056 mm | Z drive |
| GT2 20-tooth pulley, 8 mm bore | a real part with hub diameter (it must clear the 608's outer ring: at most about 18 mm) | the axial load path |
| GT2 12 mm belt and 20-tooth pulleys, 5 mm bore | a maker with data; Gates has no 12 mm in 2 mm pitch | Y drive |
| 608 bearing | maker's axial rating and internal clearance | axial load path (catalogue: "typical, unverified") |
| T8 x 2 screw and nut | lead accuracy, straightness, nut backlash and axial stiffness | synchronisation between screws |
| NEMA 17, 40 mm (17HS16-2004S1) | radial shaft-load limit | Z belt: 17.4 N at 15.2 mm, not judged |
| NEMA 17, 48 mm (17HS19-2004S1) | what "LENGTH 20mm: 21N MAX" means | Y belts |
| Hiwin MGN12 | accuracy class of the rails bought; moment rigidity of a block | level over travel, the single-block guide |
| M5 washer, 1 mm | modelled as a 1 mm spacer of unknown range | Y idler position |
| For the better Z option | integrated lead-screw motor 17E19S1684MB4-300RS: holding torque, current, resistance, inductance, rotor inertia, mass, body and nut dimensions, thrust rating; or a T8 thrust-bearing block | would remove pulleys' set screws from the load path |
